name: Taiwan
governanceModel: New AI Basic Act atop a chip-centric, not model-centric, AI economy
debateTopics: AI chip export controls on China beyond the existing US blacklist
Building an AI ecosystem around chips rather than models
overview:
Taiwan's AI Basic Act passed the Legislative Yuan in December 2025 and took effect on 14 January 2026, adopting an EU-AI-Act-aligned definition of AI and seven core principles: sustainable development and wellbeing, human autonomy, privacy, cybersecurity, transparency, fairness, and accountability. The Cabinet is now forming a national AI strategy committee to draft Taiwan's first AI development blueprint.

Unlike most peer economies profiled here, Taiwan's AI story is overwhelmingly about chips, not models — TSMC's centrality to the global AI hardware supply chain dominates its ecosystem far more than any domestic frontier AI software lab, which Taiwan notably lacks at a scale comparable to Japan's Sakana AI or France's Mistral. As of mid-2026, Taiwan is reportedly considering export-control rules on AI chips to China that go beyond the existing US blacklist, with direct implications for TSMC and its supply chain.

debates.topic: AI chip export controls on China beyond the existing US blacklist
debates.summary: Taiwan is reportedly considering export restrictions on AI chips to China that go further than current US rules — a move with direct consequences for TSMC and its server-maker customers.
debates.expanded: Because TSMC manufactures the overwhelming majority of the world's most advanced AI chips, any Taiwanese export-control decision has outsized global impact compared to a similar decision by most other governments. Server makers like Foxconn face real supply-chain risk if restrictions tighten further, while national-security advocates argue Taiwan has strong incentive to align closely with US controls given its own security relationship with Washington.

debates.topic: Building an AI ecosystem around chips rather than models
debates.summary: Taiwan's AI policy conversation is unusually dominated by hardware and supply-chain questions rather than model development or deployment risk.
debates.expanded: Unlike most economies profiled here, Taiwan doesn't have a domestic frontier AI software lab to build policy around — its AI Basic Act and strategy committee are working to define what an AI development blueprint looks like for an economy whose comparative advantage is manufacturing the chips everyone else's models run on, rather than building the models themselves.
